# MathCheck-style Robustness Evaluation — Summary

**Model (solver):** claude-sonnet-5
**Problem set:** `problems_external.json` — 12 problems generated by a separate LLM (GPT) and answer-checked with SymPy, used to reduce generator–solver overlap.
**Design:** fixed variant set (`variants_frozen.jsonl`, frozen once) solved over **5 runs**; results are mean ± std, so run-to-run variance reflects solver stochasticity only, not changing variant wording.

## Accuracy per variant (mean ± std over 5 runs)

| Variant | Mean accuracy | Std |
|---|---|---|
| original | 100.0% | 0.0 |
| problem_understanding (reword) | 98.3% | 3.3 |
| irrelevant_disturbance | 100.0% | 0.0 |
| scenario_reframe | 93.3% | 3.3 |
| **misleading_hint** | **61.7%** | **4.1** |

## Robustness drop vs. original (mean, with per-run range)

| Variant | Mean drop | Per-run range |
|---|---|---|
| problem_understanding | +1.7 pts | +0.0 to +8.3 |
| irrelevant_disturbance | +0.0 pts | +0.0 to +0.0 |
| scenario_reframe | +6.7 pts | +0.0 to +8.3 |
| **misleading_hint** | **+38.3 pts** | **+33.3 to +41.7** |

## Reading

The misleading-hint drop is large and **stable across runs** (range 33–42 pts), unlike the single-run pilot numbers earlier (which swung 8–25 pts because variants were regenerated each run). Fixing the variant set removed that confound and made the effect reproducible.

This is a **12-problem pilot** — an exploratory signal, not a general claim about frontier models. Answers are programmatically checked with SymPy where parsing succeeds; this is not a formally verified benchmark. See `misleading_hint_cases.md` for the three distinct failure mechanisms behind the drop, including one honest counter-case (correct hint, model still wrong).
